CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury sustained during basketball.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male presents with right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son. Patient went up for a shot and was contacted by his son while in the air. Upon landing, patient rolled and twisted his ankle. Patient reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient reports difficulty walking and sensation of ankle instability. Patient notes he recently returned to a regular workout routine at the gym. X-ray obtained today shows displaced lateral malleolus fracture at the Weber C level with no evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. On examination, exquisite tenderness laterally over the lateral malleolus and some tenderness over the medial deltoid region. Swelling on the lateral side of ankle noted. Skin intact with brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Patient able to stand but unable to walk comfortably due to pain and instability.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. Recently returned to regular gym workouts. Plays basketball with his 10-year-old son. Volunteered to coach basketball starting in April. Has dogs at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right ankle: Exquisite tenderness laterally. Tenderness over medial deltoid region. Swelling on lateral side. Skin intact. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Patient able to stand but reports instability with weight-bearing.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture of right ankle, Weber C, displaced with instability. Requires surgical intervention with plate and screw fixation. Patient to be non-weight bearing and provided with crutches. Meloxicam prescribed for pain and swelling management. Patient instructed to ice ankle and keep elevated regularly. Patient able to work from home which will facilitate ankle elevation. Expected recovery time approximately three months. Patient cleared to continue coaching starting in April. Follow-up to initiate gradual return to exercise within three-month timeframe.
